# SOOS — Cross-Principal Agent Communication (PEER)
# draft-sato-soos-peer-00
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/peer/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: 2026-06-30

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

PEER (Cross-Principal Agent Communication) is the SOOS protocol for
governing transactions between two AI agents that each operate under
independent mandate roots, independent Governed Execution Contexts
(GECs), and independent audit chains. PEER introduces the PEER
Transaction Record (PTR) as a new first-class SOOS primitive, and
the ptxn_id (Cross-Principal Transaction ID) as a jointly-derived
correlation identifier that links two independent GAR audit chains
at the moment of a cross-principal transaction.

PEER is NOT: a sub-agent orchestration protocol (that is MAD/SACR);
a cross-principal constitutional layer (each GEC's CAP governs only
its own side); a business payload specification (domain protocols
such as ATP govern the payload); or a dispute resolution mechanism
(OQ-PEER-03, deferred to PEER-01).

draft-sato-soos-peer-00 is a problem statement and architecture draft.
Normative ALE schemas, full PTR field specifications, and dispute
resolution procedures are deferred to draft-sato-soos-peer-01
(post-Vienna, IETF 126).

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

Without PEER, two independently-governed AI agents that transact
with each other produce two separate audit records with no shared
identifier. An auditor cannot confirm that Record A and Record B
describe the same transaction. A party can deny participation. A
forged audit entry claiming a transaction occurred (or did not occur)
is undetectable.

The Provenance Paradox (arXiv:2603.18043) demonstrates this
empirically: self-reported quality scores in multi-agent routing
perform worse than random (0.55 vs. 0.68 mean quality score,
p<0.001). Honor-system self-certification fails adversarially.

PEER replaces self-certification with a cryptographic mutual
attestation handshake and a jointly-derived ptxn_id that neither
agent can produce without the other's participation. Both GAR chains
independently record the ptxn_id. An auditor holding both chains
can reconstruct the cross-principal transaction by matching ptxn_id
values and verifying the responding GEC countersignature.

The design premise: the audit boundary does not stop at the edge of
your own GEC. Cross-principal transactions are only auditable if
both sides' records are provably linked — and that link must not
require trusting either party's self-report.

---

## SECTION 3 — Key Normative Concepts

[NEW in -00] Cross-Principal Transaction:
A transaction between two AI agents each operating under an
independent mandate root, where neither agent's principal is the
same entity as, or a delegate of, the other agent's principal, and
no shared Governed Execution Context (GEC) governs both sides.

[NEW in -00] PEER:
The Cross-Principal Agent Communication protocol defined in
draft-sato-soos-peer-00. PEER governs the attestation, gating, and
audit correlation requirements for a Cross-Principal Transaction.
PEER does not govern the business payload of the transaction.

[NEW in -00] PEER Transaction Record (PTR):
A jointly-produced governance artifact capturing the identities,
timestamp, correlation identifier, and pre-call gate references for
a Cross-Principal Transaction. The PTR is produced by both GECs
independently and stored in each party's GAR chain. The PTR is not
a business record; it is a governance correlation record.

[NEW in -00] ptxn_id (Cross-Principal Transaction ID):
A deterministically-derived identifier produced by the Initiating
Agent's GEC and countersigned by the Responding Agent's GEC,
uniquely identifying a single Cross-Principal Transaction. Derived
as:
  ptxn_id = UUID-v5(
    initiating_kia_id || responding_kia_id || initiated_at ||
    initiating_nonce  || responding_nonce
  )
Neither party can produce a valid ptxn_id without the other's
nonce contribution.

[NEW in -00] Initiating Agent:
The agent that opens a Cross-Principal Transaction by presenting its
KIA identity and requesting the Responding Agent's participation.
The Initiating Agent's GEC generates the ptxn_id.

[NEW in -00] Responding Agent:
The agent that receives a Cross-Principal Transaction request,
validates the Initiating Agent's KIA identity, and countersigns the
ptxn_id to confirm mutual participation.

[NEW in -00] ALE-PEER (candidate event types — normative schemas
deferred to PEER-01):
  ALE-PEER-01: MUTUAL_ATTESTATION_COMPLETE
  ALE-PEER-02: PTXN_ID_ISSUED
  ALE-PEER-03: PEER_TRANSACTION_COMPLETE
  ALE-PEER-04: PEER_ATTESTATION_FAILED

---

## SECTION 4 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

draft-kuehlewind-audit-architecture-00 (Kühlewind/Birkholz,
Ericsson/Fraunhofer, May 2026): Defines an architecture for
auditing AI agent delegation, identifying six Potential Work Items
(WI-1 through WI-6). SOOS GAR (draft-sato-soos-gar-03) provides
normative implementations of WI-1, WI-4, WI-5, and WI-6. PEER
addresses the cross-domain case their draft explicitly does not
solve: "correlation emerges from consistent use of shared
identifiers across all participants" fails when participants have
independent GECs.

draft-prakash-aip-00 (AIP): Invocation-Bound Capability Tokens
(IBCT) at the transport layer. AIP IBCT is a candidate transport
token for the PEER mutual attestation handshake. AIP and PEER
compose at the transport/session boundary; they do not compete.
The Provenance Paradox (arXiv:2603.18043) by the same author is
cited in PEER §1 as empirical motivation for kernel-enforced
attestation.

arXiv:2603.18043 (Provenance Paradox, Prakash 2026): Demonstrates
that self-reported quality scores in multi-agent systems perform
worse than random. Cited in PEER §1 as the empirical baseline
establishing that honor-system delegation fails adversarially.

draft-klrc-aiagent-auth-02 (AIMS, Kasselman et al.): AI agent
authentication via WIMSE + SPIFFE + OAuth. PEER begins after
authentication is established; AIMS and PEER compose at the
authentication/session boundary.

WIMSE (draft-ietf-wimse-workload-identity): Workload identity
substrate. KIA (draft-sato-soos-kia-03) is compatible with WIMSE
identity substrates and is the persistent identity layer PEER uses.

---

## SECTION 5 — Normative SOOS Cross-References

This draft depends on:
  KIA-03    (draft-sato-soos-kia-03) — persistent agent identity;
              mutual attestation handshake uses KIA
  AEP-02    (draft-sato-soos-aep-02) — session governance; PTR
              carried as AEP session metadata; ptxn_id in ALE fields
  GAR-03    (draft-sato-soos-gar-03) — audit record; ALE-PEER-01
              through ALE-PEER-04 candidate registration
  RGP-00    (draft-sato-soos-rgp-00) — capability discovery pre-call
              gate; rgp_resource_id in PTR
  ACD-00    (draft-sato-soos-acd-00) — compliance disclosure pre-call
              gate; acd_session_id in PTR (conditional)
  KEE-00    (draft-sato-soos-kee-00) — ptxn_id derivation function
              added as minor kernel API extension

The following drafts depend on this draft (post-Vienna):
  PEER-01   (draft-sato-soos-peer-01) — full normative specification
  FAIP-[TBD] — federated multi-agent pools; FAIP agents in
              cross-principal transactions use PEER (OQ-PEER-08)
